correctness.rationale: At fixed \(0<\phi<\pi\) the compact zero-band states have positive invertible tridiagonal Gram matrix with inverse kernel \((1+r^2)(-r)^{|i-j|}/(1-r^2)\). Two defect plaquettes give a four-dimensional rank reduction with matrix blocks \(D=\operatorname{diag}((1+r)/2,(1-r)/2)\) and cross-block \(t\begin{psmallmatrix}-1&-1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(|t|=(1-r^2)r^{d-1}/4\). Symbolic determinant equals \(\big[(x-1/2)^2-r^2/4\big]^2-4t^2(x-1/2)^2\), providing four exact eigenvalues and each same-branch splitting \(2|t|\). The isolated flat-band perturbation expansion yields epsilon times these eigenvalues plus \(O(\varepsilon^2)\), at fixed parameters; no nonzero-strength equality is claimed. Standalone verification reconstructed exact compact states, checked symbolic determinant, six independent projected finite sections and twelve full finite-chain spectra. The proof does not infer infinite conclusions from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The closest original source, Viedma et al. arXiv:2407.15789v1, Appendix A, directly measures two-plaquette coupling numerically and describes high/low couplings as approximately equal; it does not state the exact four-level secular factorization or common prefactor. Marques et al. arXiv:2407.14405v1 gives a single-impurity-plaquette two-level compression, whose doublet energies are recovered when pair separation tends to infinity, but not the finite-separation four-level spectrum. Searches for exact two-pair coupling laws, aliases, inverse Gram Toeplitz formulations and stronger multi-impurity coverage found no claiming theorem. Residual risk: a related 2024 doctoral thesis was indexed but its full text could not be read.
residual_risks: The related 2024 doctoral thesis was not read in full; it may contain additional derivations.
A mathematical re-expression of the four-level spectrum could conceivably occur in a less obviously titled prior work, despite searched aliases and close primary inspection.

value.rationale: The primary two-pair experiment establishes the physically motivated quantitative question and explicitly finds high/lower branch near-equality surprising. The exact four-root law proves equal first-order tunneling despite different mode extents, gives the full flux- and separation-dependent prefactor and reproduces its 0.17 coupling-ratio measurement as \(3-2\sqrt2\). This is relevant to matching effective SSH channel couplings, not an arbitrary slice, known-table recalculation or unmotivated improvement in numeric precision. The theorem does not claim broad many-impurity topology.
